title: Share a published-content projection across public delivery channels
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a publication operator, I want feeds and application delivery to reflect the same published content, so that visibility and updates are consistent across channels.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Share a published-content projection across public delivery channels
  Scenario: Publish, revise and withdraw an article
    Given a publication with a published article and a private newer draft
    When a reader requests its subscription feed or application representation
    Then both expose the same current published version and canonical identity
    And neither exposes the newer draft or private editorial data
    When a published revision or withdrawal is made
    Then both reflect that change within a documented freshness bound
    And an older delayed update cannot restore withdrawn or superseded public content
  Scenario: Keep publication boundaries
    Given two separately configured publications
    When public content is projected for one publication
    Then only that publication's eligible published content and public assets are included
```

Foundation dependency for both delivery epics. Later implementation must inspect and reuse the existing Published* lifecycle, ContentRepository, Markus/S3 projection and incremental reconciliation/invalidation behavior; do not build another publishing engine. Review current docs/public-surface.md, docs/site-hosting.md, projection/public_data.py and M8 PPY-f293ea. Existing latest/search JSON is not yet a versioned article-body delivery contract. Define explicit public field and asset allowlists; do not blindly expose metadata/frontMatterYaml or editorial internals. Define common eligibility, channel opt-outs, canonical IDs/URLs, published revision timestamps, withdrawal and cache/reconciliation behavior. Transport and hosting choices remain design work.

Approved platform scope: whenever saving a content item changes publicly published content, automatically refresh its article representation, affected listings/indexes, sitemap, RSS and Atom, plus headless outputs when enabled. Publish, published edits and unpublish share the same content selection and metadata rules; private draft saves never enter public outputs. Failures of ancillary projections must be visible and retryable. Definition of Done includes the child post-save behavior story, published-only isolation, common identity/update selection and documented consistency/failure contracts. Orchestration, atomicity and transport details remain design decisions; no new services are prescribed. Promoted from story to epic solely to provide a schema-valid parent for the approved child behavior; ID, parent initiative, existing dependencies and implementation-unstarted status are preserved.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Approved planning-only extension: PPY-defff04e-17b5-4e28-9bb5-df412601a102 specifies general automatic post-save public projection, including article/listings/indexes, sitemap, both RSS/Atom and enabled headless delivery, with private-draft isolation and visible/retryable ancillary failures. Foundation retains ID PPY-3f55c3e1-65f6-4fc7-833e-6cecc6a85270 and is now an epic because Kanbus forbids story parents. Both delivery epics depend explicitly on the new story as well as this foundation; their guides and cross-cutting delivery review were updated. Existing M3 projection evidence is linked, not replaced. No implementation, one-site sitemap audit or new service prescribed. Discussion that RSS/Atom is simplest first and Monitoring has greater benefit is prioritization context only, not coding authorization.
